findings.summary: Rebase section shows a flattened fragment list and code before the one-line idea, so the replay process is not presented as a clear diagram or step flow.
findings.evidence: "Take commits" / "main..feature" / "Replay one by one" / "on the new tip" / "New SHAs" / "linear history" / "Old commits" / "orphaned" followed by the bash block
findings.fix: State the idea in one line first ("Rebase replays feature's commits onto main's tip"), then show a before/after diagram of the branch graph with the old commits marked orphaned.

findings.summary: The two interview answers about flags are written as question-and-answer prose lines rather than bullets or table rows, and the 'Silent default' note repeats the --no-ff row.
findings.evidence: "Why --no-ff? ff is possible, but you want the branch visible." and "Plain git merge fast-forwards silently. Use --no-ff to keep the branch bubble."
findings.fix: Drop the duplicate note and keep the flags only in the table, or fold the Q&A into one-line bullets.

findings.summary: Page 3 contains two ideas in the 'Undo and Publish' block, with a force-push bullet that mixes the action and its warning, and the reflog undo is shown as a bullet list plus code.
findings.evidence: "Update it with git push --force-with-lease. Never plain --force: it can overwrite a teammate's new commits."
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: one for the command to use, one for why plain --force is unsafe.

findings.summary: The verb table for squash and fixup shows the same effect text for both, and the squash-vs-fixup distinction is only in a trailing prose sentence.
findings.evidence: "squash (s) | melt into previous commit | combined" and "fixup (f) | melt into previous commit | discarded"; "Both fold into the previous commit. squash keeps both messages; fixup keeps only the earlier one."
findings.fix: Remove the redundant trailing sentence or reduce it to the table, and keep the Message column as the distinguishing cue.

findings.summary: The 'Shared branch already rebased?' section lists Fix, Check and Remember as terse labels without explaining the recovery steps, so a skimming learner cannot tell what to do.
findings.evidence: "Fix / git pull --rebase / Check / git reflog / Remember / Rebase private history, merge shared history."
findings.fix: Rewrite as short ordered steps: 1) run git pull --rebase to replay local work onto the rewritten branch, 2) use git reflog to find lost commits if something went missing.

findings.summary: The pull.rebase and pull.ff config bullets are two separate options presented together, with 'pick one default' only in a code comment, so the relationship is unclear.
findings.evidence: "pull.rebase true makes rebase the default pull" / "pull.ff only makes a pull fail instead of merging" / "pick one default"
findings.fix: State in a bullet that these are alternatives (rebase on pull vs fail on divergence) and show a small two-row table.
